dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:7701.text: A neighborhood gate. Formed from 門, with 呂 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: 'Five households form a 比; five 比 form a 閭.' 閭 means companions: twenty-five households group together as companions.

shuowen:7702.text: A gate within a neighborhood. Formed from 門, with 臽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7703.text: The outer gate of a market. Formed from 門, with 貴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7704.text: An inner, successive gate within a city. Formed from 門, with 垔 indicating the sound. The Odes says: 'Going out through its gate towers.'

shuowen:7705.text: The gate structure expressed by 闉闍. Formed from 門, with 者 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7706.text: A gate tower. Formed from 門, with 欮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7707.text: A gate's supporting bracket. Formed from 門, with 弁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7708.text: A door leaf. Formed from 門, with 介 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7709.text: A door leaf. Alternatively, to close. Formed from 門, with 盍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7710.text: A gate's central post. Formed from 門, with 臬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7711.text: A threshold. Formed from 門, with 或 indicating the sound. The Analects says: 'When walking, he did not tread on the threshold.'

shuowen:7712.text: A gate being high. Formed from 門, with 良 indicating the sound. There is a 閬中 county in Ba commandery.

shuowen:7713.text: To open. Formed from 門, with 辟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7714.text: To open a gate. Formed from 門, with 爲 indicating the sound. The Discourses of the States says: 'He opened the gate and spoke with him.'

shuowen:7715.text: To open. Formed from 門, with 單 indicating the sound. The Changes says: 'Make the hidden manifest.'

shuowen:7716.text: To open wide. Formed from 門 and 幵.

shuowen:7717.text: To open. Formed from 門, with 豈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7718.text: To open wide. Formed from 門, with 可 indicating the sound. A large cup is also called 閜.

shuowen:7719.text: To open and close a gate. Formed from 門, with 甲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7720.text: To shut a gate. Formed from 門, with 必 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: 'He shut the gate and spoke with him.'

shuowen:7721.text: Something used to stop a door leaf. Formed from 門, with 各 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7722.text: A gap. Formed from 門 and 月.

shuowen:7723.text: A gate tilting. Formed from 門, with 阿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7724.text: To obstruct and block. Formed from 門, with 於 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7725.text: A gate opening and closing smoothly. Formed from 門, with 繇 indicating the sound. Alternatively, ten strands of thread, expressed by 縷十紘; the technical wording is uncertain.

shuowen:7726.text: The sound of a gate. Formed from 門, with 曷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7727.text: A gate's resounding sound. Formed from 門, with 郷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7728.text: A gate's barrier. Formed from 門, with 柬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7729.text: A barrier. Formed from 木 within 門.

shuowen:7730.text: To close a gate. Formed from 門; 才 is what bars the gate.

shuowen:7731.text: To close from outside. Formed from 門, with 亥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7732.text: To close a gate. Formed from 門, with 音 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7733.text: To hold a gate or door shut with a crosswise piece of wood. Formed from 門, with 𢇅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7734.text: The male peg below a gate-bar. Formed from 門, with 龠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7735.text: An abundant appearance. Formed from 門, with 眞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7736.text: 闛闛 is an abundant appearance. Formed from 門, with 堂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7737.text: A eunuch servant: a palace eunuch gatekeeper who closes the gates. Formed from 門, with 奄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7738.text: A servant who regularly closes the gate at dusk. Formed from 門 and 昏; 昏 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:7739.text: To peep. Formed from 門, with 規 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7740.text: To enter the palace precincts without permission. Formed from 門, with 䜌 indicating the sound. Read like 闌.

shuowen:7741.text: To ascend. Formed from 門 and 𠄟. 𠄟 is ancient-script 下. Read like 敶 in 軍敶, 'army formation.'

shuowen:7742.text: To put one's head through a gate and peep. Formed from 人 within 門.

shuowen:7743.text: To count everything within a gate. Formed from 門, with abbreviated 說 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7744.text: When business is finished, to close the gate. Formed from 門, with 癸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7745.text: To look out. Formed from 門, with 敢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7746.text: Spacious or widely separated. Formed from 門, with 𣴠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7747.text: A mourner at the gate. Formed from 門, with 文 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7748.text: The appearance of a horse coming out of a gate. Formed from 馬 within 門. Read like 郴.

shuowen:7749.text: A market wall. Formed from 門, with 瞏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7750.text: A gate. Formed from 門, with 達 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7751.text: 閌閬 means a lofty gate. Formed from 門, with 亢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7752.text: 閥閱 means to recount one's own merits. Formed from 門, with 伐 indicating the sound. In this sense 伐 should be used interchangeably.

shuowen:7753.text: Quiet. Formed from 門, with 狊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7754.text: That which governs hearing. A pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 耳.

shuowen:7755.text: A drooping ear. Formed from 耳 hanging downward; a pictograph. The Spring and Autumn Commentary's 'Prince Zhe of Qin' had drooping ears and was named accordingly.

shuowen:7756.text: Small drooping ears. Formed from 耳, with 占 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7757.text: Large, drooping ears. Formed from 耳, with 冘 indicating the sound. The Odes says: 'When the gentleman becomes engrossed.'

shuowen:7758.text: Long ears. Formed from 耳, with 冉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7759.text: Drooping ears. Formed from 耳, with 詹 indicating the sound. In the south is the country of Drooping Ears.

shuowen:7760.text: Ears attached to the cheeks. Formed from 耳, with abbreviated 烓 indicating the sound. Du Lin says 耿 means light, formed from 光 and abbreviated 聖. In characters the form component is on the left and the sound component on the right; Du Lin is wrong.

shuowen:7761.text: To connect. Formed from 耳, since ears connect to the cheeks, and 絲, since silk threads connect without interruption.

shuowen:7762.text: Ringing in the ears. Formed from 耳, with 卯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7763.text: To understand comprehensively. Formed from 耳, with 呈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7764.text: Perceptive. Formed from 耳, with 怱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7765.text: To listen. Formed from 耳 and 㥁, with 壬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7766.text: To listen. Formed from 耳, with 令 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7767.text: To record subtle matters. Formed from 耳, with 戠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7768.text: Noisy or cheerful talking. Formed from 耳, with 𠯑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7769.text: To strain the ears to hear something. Formed from 耳, with 禹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7770.text: Sound. Formed from 耳, with 殸 indicating the sound. 殸 is the large-seal form of 磬.

shuowen:7771.text: To know by hearing. Formed from 耳, with 門 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7772.text: To visit or inquire. Formed from 耳, with 甹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7773.text: Unable to hear. Formed from 耳, with 龍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7774.text: Deaf from birth is called 聳. Formed from 耳, with abbreviated 從 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7775.text: In the provinces of Yi and Liang, deafness is called 䏁; in Qin and Jin, listening without hearing, or hearing without understanding, is called 䏁. Formed from 耳, with 宰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7776.text: Deaf. Formed from 耳, with 貴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7777.text: Without understanding. Formed from 耳, with 出 indicating the sound. Read like 孽.

shuowen:7778.text: Beyond Wu and Chu, anyone without ears is called 𦘍, spoken as though the ears had been cut off for a covenant. Formed from 耳, with 闋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7779.text: Under military law, to pierce an ear with an arrow. Formed from 耳 and 矢. The Methods of the Sima says: 'For a small offense, pierce the ear; a middle offense, amputate the feet; a grave offense, cut the throat.'

shuowen:7780.text: Ears severed in battle. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: 'To make them captives and severed ears.' Formed from 耳, with 或 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7781.text: An ear falling off. Formed from 耳, with 月 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7782.text: The ears of the golden horse on the imperial carriage, apparently. Formed from 耳, with 麻 indicating the sound. Read like 渳 in 渳水; alternatively, like 靡 in the Monthly Ordinances' 靡草.

shuowen:7783.text: The Discourses of the States says: 'Huilu lodged at 耹遂.' The explanation is lacking.

shuowen:7784.text: At peace. Formed from two 耳.

shuowen:7785.text: To whisper quietly at another's ear. Formed from three 耳.

shuowen:7786.text: Not to listen. Formed from 耳, with 敖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7787.text: The jaw or chin, as in 𩔞. A pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 𦣞.

shuowen:7788.text: A broad jaw. Formed from 𦣞, with 巳 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7789.text: A fist or hand. A pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 手.

shuowen:7790.text: The middle of the hand. Formed from 手, with 尚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7791.text: The chief finger, the thumb. Formed from 手, with 母 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7792.text: A finger of the hand. Formed from 手, with 旨 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7793.text: A hand or fist. Formed from 手, with  indicating the sound.

shuowen:7794.text: The wrist of the hand. Yang Xiong says: '𢯲 means to grasp.' Formed from 手, with 𥄗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7795.text: The appearance of beautiful hands. The Odes says: 'Slender and beautiful are your hands.' Formed from 手, with 韱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7796.text: The appearance of a person's arm. Formed from 手, with 削 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: 'The spokes should have that tapering shape.'

shuowen:7797.text: To lift or gather up. Alternatively, to lift one's robe to ascend the hall. Formed from 手, with 區 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7798.text: To lift one's robe. Formed from 手, with 褰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7799.text: To raise and lower the hands in salutation. Formed from 手, with 壹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7800.text: To push aside or extend. Formed from 手, with 咠 indicating the sound. Alternatively, placing the hands against the chest is called 揖.
